However, this certainty naturally diminishes over time. The 1-week interval widens considerably to [87.11, 95.14], accommodating more potential variability over a longer period. Several specific risks or unforeseen events could push actual outcomes outside these stated intervals. Even a series of smaller, unpredicted events accumulating over a month could collectively lead to a deviation that falls outside the 90% confidence range. Given that the 1-month upper bound is close to 100, a particularly strong positive surge driven by an unanticipated catalyst might push outcomes to the very top or even slightly beyond the forecasted interval.
